findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the unit-test description in the Testing section to assert that each of the five moves is accompanied by a recognizable example block (e.g., assert a `Before:` / `After:` label or a fenced code block appears within N characters of each move name).

findings.finding: The Testing section asserts 'each of the five move names appears with an example block', and AC1 requires 'each with an example block (checked: unit test asserting section and move names)' — but the described unit test only asserts section existence and move names, not the presence of an example block per move. A test that greps for move names alone can pass even if all five example blocks are absent, making AC1's 'each with an example block' claim unverified.
scenarios: An executor adds move names without any before/after examples; the unit test passes but the guide never demonstrates the technique, defeating the guide's purpose.
A reviewer cannot distinguish a name-only entry from a fully worked example via the described test.
findings.suggested_fix: In tests/test_guides.py, after asserting each move name, add a pattern like `assert re.search(r'specification-by-example.*?```', content, re.DOTALL)` (anchored to the section) or assert that the string 'Before:' (or '```') follows each move name within the section, so the test fails when examples are missing.

AC3 enforces exact-spelling via a unit test that imports coach_moves, but if the executor writes hyphenated headings throughout the guide section, the test will catch it only at test-time — the spec itself contains no positive instruction on the naming form, creating an instruction-locality gap.
